Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Fungal infection by Venturia inaequalis. Spreads in cool, wet spring weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown scabby lesions on leaves and fruit. Leaves may curl and drop early.
chemical_treatments: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L water at pink bud stage
Apply Captan 50% WP @ 3 g/L at 10-day intervals
Use Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1 g/L if infection is heavy
organic_treatments: Wettable sulfur spray every 7-10 days
Neem oil spray 5ml/L water on affected leaves
Remove and destroy fallen infected leaves
Ensure proper tree spacing for good air circulation
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Rake and dispose fallen leaves. Prune for good air circulation.

Apple___Black_rot.cause: Fungal disease by Botryosphaeria obtusa. Enters through wounds.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown rings on fruit that expand. Leaves show purple spots. Cankers on branches.
chemical_treatments: Apply Captan 50% WP @ 3 g/L every 10-14 days
Use Thiophanate-methyl 70% WP @ 1.5 g/L for canker control
organic_treatments: Prune out infected branches 15 cm below visible infection
Bordeaux mixture (1:1:10) spray after pruning
Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L as protective spray
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummified fruits. Cut out cankered wood. Disinfect pruning tools.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae. Requires juniper/cedar and apple to complete lifecycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on upper leaf surface. Pale orange tubes on leaf undersides.
chemical_treatments: Apply Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1 g/L at pink bud stage
Spray Triadimefon 25% WP @ 1 g/L every 7-10 days in wet weather
organic_treatments: Remove nearby juniper/cedar trees if possible
Sulfur-based fungicide sprays every 7 days from bud break
Neem oil 5 ml/L water spray on new growth
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Plant rust-resistant apple varieties. Remove juniper galls in spring.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with normal green foliage.
chemical_treatments: No treatment needed — plant is healthy!
organic_treatments: Continue regular fertilization and irrigation
Monitor periodically for early signs of pests or disease
Apple___healthy.prevention: Maintain good orchard hygiene, proper spacing, and balanced fertilization.

chemical_treatments: No treatment needed
organic_treatments: Regular watering and mulching

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.cause: Caused by Podosphaera clandestina fungus. Spreads in warm days and cool nights.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on young leaves and shoots. Leaves curl, turn brown, and drop.
chemical_treatments: Spray Sulfur 80% WP @ 3 g/L water every 10 days
Apply Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1 g/L at first sign of disease
Use Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 ml/L for severe infections
organic_treatments: Baking soda spray: 5g + 5ml dish soap per liter water
Neem oil 5ml/L water on affected parts
Prune overcrowded branches for better air circulation
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen. Prune for good air circulation. Plant resistant varieties.

chemical_treatments: No treatment needed
organic_treatments: Continue standard care practices
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Regular monitoring and good orchard hygiene.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.cause: Caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis fungus. Favored by warm, humid, cloudy weather.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular gray-to-tan lesions parallel to leaf veins. Lesions may merge causing large dead areas.
chemical_treatments: Apply Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L water at VT stage
Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.5 ml/L at first symptom
Use Pyraclostrobin 20% WG @ 0.5 g/L for heavy infections
organic_treatments: Crop rotation — avoid maize-maize rotation for 2+ years
Deep plow infected crop residue after harvest
Use Trichoderma viride 1% WP @ 2.5 kg/ha as soil treatment
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids. Rotate crops. Avoid overhead irrigation.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cause: Caused by Puccinia sorghi fungus. Spread by wind-blown spores.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Oval to elongated pustules on both leaf surfaces, brick-red to dark brown in color.
chemical_treatments: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L water at rust appearance
Apply Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 ml/L every 10-14 days
organic_treatments: Plant resistant hybrid varieties
Sulfur-based fungicide spray as preventive measure
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Use resistant hybrids. Early planting can help avoid peak rust periods.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Caused by Setosphaeria turcica. Favored by moderate temperatures and high humidity.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Large cigar-shaped gray-green to tan lesions (2.5-15 cm long) on leaves with wavy margins.
chemical_treatments: Apply Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L at first sign
Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.5 ml/L every 14 days
Use Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L as protective spray
organic_treatments: Crop rotation with non-grass crops for 1-2 years
Deep plow infected residue immediately after harvest
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Crop rotation. Proper residue management.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with normal green leaves.
chemical_treatments: No treatment needed
organic_treatments: Continue proper irrigation and fertilization schedule
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops annually. Use certified disease-free seeds.

Grape___Black_rot.cause: Caused by Guignardia bidwellii fungus. Most destructive in warm, humid weather.
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Circular brown spots on leaves with dark border. Infected berries turn black and shriveled.
chemical_treatments: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L water from budbreak
Spray Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1 g/L every 10-14 days
Use Captan 50% WP @ 3 g/L after heavy rainfall
organic_treatments: Remove and destroy all infected clusters and mummified berries
Copper hydroxide 77% WP @ 3 g/L spray
Improve canopy airflow through proper pruning and trellising
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Remove mummified berries. Prune for airflow. Begin spray program at budbreak.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: Complex wood disease caused by Phaeomoniella chlamydospora and Phaeoacremonium fungi.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe pattern on leaves. Dark berries with black spots. Sudden vine collapse possible.
chemical_treatments: No fully effective chemical control for wood phase
Thiophanate-methyl 70% WP @ 1.5 g/L on pruning cuts as wound protectant
Bordeaux mixture applied immediately after pruning
organic_treatments: Remove infected wood well below visible symptoms
Protect pruning wounds immediately with wound sealants
Remove and destroy severely affected vines
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Prune during dry weather. Seal large pruning wounds.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.cause: Caused by Pseudocercospora vitis fungus. Common in warm, moist climates.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on upper leaf surface. Whitish sporulation on lower leaf surface.
chemical_treatments: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L water every 10-14 days
Apply Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1 g/L for active infections
Use Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L as protective spray
organic_treatments: Remove infected leaves and dispose away from vineyard
Bordeaux mixture (1:1:100) spray every 14 days
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Proper pruning for air circulation. Avoid overhead irrigation. Remove fallen leaves.

chemical_treatments: No treatment needed
organic_treatments: Continue regular pruning and canopy management
Grape___healthy.prevention: Good vineyard hygiene and proper pruning practices.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Caused by Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus bacteria. Spread by Asian citrus psyllid. Incurable.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Yellow mottling of leaves. Small, lopsided, bitter fruit. Premature fruit drop.
chemical_treatments: CRITICAL: No cure — infected trees must be removed and destroyed immediately
Control psyllid vector: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5 ml/L
Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L spray for psyllid control
organic_treatments: Remove and burn infected trees immediately to prevent spread
Kaolin clay spray to deter psyllid feeding
Neem oil 5ml/L spray to repel psyllid insects
Release Tamarixia radiata (parasitic wasp) for biological control
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Use certified disease-free nursery stock. Control psyllid populations.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.cause: Caused by Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni bacteria. Spread by rain and wind.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown with yellow halo. Fruit lesions with raised borders.
chemical_treatments: Apply Copper hydroxide 77% WP @ 3 g/L starting at bud swell
Spray Oxytetracycline HCl 22% SP @ 0.5 g/L during bloom
Use Kasugamycin 8% SL @ 1.5 ml/L for active infection
organic_treatments: Copper sulfate 25% WP @ 2.5 g/L spray
Prune out infected shoots 20 cm below visible symptoms
Avoid overhead irrigation to reduce leaf wetness
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Use copper sprays preventively. Avoid wounding trees.

chemical_treatments: No treatment needed
organic_treatments: Continue regular pruning and monitoring
Peach___healthy.prevention: Annual dormant copper sprays, good drainage, disease-resistant varieties.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.cause: Caused by Xanthomonas euvesicatoria bacteria. Spreads through rain splash and infected seeds.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves turning brown with yellow margins. Raised, scabby lesions on fruit.
chemical_treatments: Spray Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L every 7-10 days
Apply Streptomycin sulfate 90% SP @ 0.5 g/L during early infection
Use Kasugamycin 8% SL @ 1.5 ml/L in combination with copper
organic_treatments: Use certified disease-free seeds or hot water treated seeds
Copper-based bactericide spray
Remove and destroy infected plant material immediately
Avoid working in field when plants are wet
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use resistant varieties. Treat seeds before planting. Rotate crops for 2-3 years.

chemical_treatments: No treatment needed
organic_treatments: Regular fertilization with balanced NPK
Proper irrigation management
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Crop rotation and use of certified disease-free seeds.

Potato___Early_blight.cause: Caused by Alternaria solani fungus. Common in warm weather with alternating dry and wet periods.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with yellow halo and concentric ring pattern (target-board appearance) on older leaves.
chemical_treatments: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L water every 7-10 days
Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L water
Use Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L for systemic control
Dithane M-45 @ 2.5 g/L as preventive spray
organic_treatments: Remove and destroy infected leaves immediately
Neem oil 5ml/L spray every 7 days
Trichoderma harzianum 1.5% WP @ 2.5 kg/ha (soil application)
Avoid overhead irrigation
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Use certified seed potatoes. Crop rotation for 3+ years. Remove plant debris.

Potato___Late_blight.cause: Caused by Phytophthora infestans. Caused the Irish potato famine. Spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions on leaves expanding rapidly. White sporulation on lesion undersides. Tuber rot with reddish-brown discoloration.
chemical_treatments: URGENT: Spray Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb 68% WP @ 2.5 g/L immediately
Apply Cymoxanil + Mancozeb 72% WP @ 3 g/L every 5-7 days
Use Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1 g/L alternated with contact fungicides
Dithane M-45 @ 2.5 g/L water as protective spray
organic_treatments: Bordeaux mixture (1:1:100) spray immediately
Remove infected plants and burn them - DO NOT compost
Destroy all infected tubers completely
Ensure good soil drainage to prevent tuber infection
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant certified blight-free seed potatoes. Resistant varieties. Good drainage.

chemical_treatments: No treatment needed
organic_treatments: Continue good agronomic practices
Potato___healthy.prevention: Use certified seed potatoes and rotate crops annually.

chemical_treatments: No treatment needed
organic_treatments: Regular pruning and proper spacing for airflow
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Prune out old canes annually. Plant in well-drained soil.

chemical_treatments: No treatment needed
organic_treatments: Continue proper irrigation and weed management
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Crop rotation, disease-resistant varieties, and proper spacing.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.cause: Caused by Podosphaera xanthii and Erysiphe cichoracearum fungi. Spreads in warm dry weather.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves and stems. Leaves may yellow and dry up. Reduces fruit quality.
chemical_treatments: Spray Sulfur 80% WP @ 3 g/L water every 10-14 days
Apply Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1 g/L at first symptom
Use Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L for systemic control
organic_treatments: Baking soda + neem oil spray: 5g baking soda + 5ml neem oil per liter
Potassium bicarbonate 15g/L water spray
Remove badly infected leaves immediately
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Avoid overhead irrigation. Ensure proper spacing.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.cause: Caused by Diplocarpon earliana fungus. Thrives in warm, wet weather.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Dark purple irregular spots on leaves with reddish-purple margins. Severely infected leaves look scorched.
chemical_treatments: Apply Captan 50% WP @ 3 g/L water every 10-14 days
Spray Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1 g/L at first symptom
organic_treatments: Remove and destroy infected leaves throughout the season
Copper hydroxide 77% WP @ 3 g/L spray
Avoid overhead irrigation
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Plant certified disease-free runners. Avoid wet foliage conditions.

chemical_treatments: No treatment needed
organic_treatments: Regular mulching to keep fruit off soil
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Use certified runners. Renovate plantings annually.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Caused by Xanthomonas vesicatoria bacteria. Spread by rain splash and infected transplants.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown with yellow halo. Raised scabby lesions on fruit. Leaf drop in severe cases.
chemical_treatments: Spray Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L water every 7 days
Apply Streptomycin sulfate 90% SP @ 0.5 g/L + Copper
Use Kasugamycin 8% SL @ 1.5 ml/L for moderate infections
organic_treatments: Use disease-free certified seeds
Bordeaux mixture (1:1:100) spray every 7-10 days
Remove infected plant material and dispose away from field
Avoid overhead irrigation
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use resistant varieties. Treat seeds with hot water. Crop rotation 2-3 years.

Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Caused by Alternaria solani. Affects tomatoes in warm (24-29C), humid weather.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target-board pattern) on older leaves. Yellow halo around spots. Stem lesions at soil line (collar rot).
chemical_treatments: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L water every 7-10 days
Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L as protective spray
Use Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L for systemic action
Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1 g/L for collar rot
organic_treatments: Remove infected lower leaves immediately and destroy
Neem oil 5ml/L water — spray every 7 days
Trichoderma viride 1.5% WP @ 2.5 kg/ha (soil drench)
Copper-based spray as preventive measure
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds. Crop rotation 3 years. Mulch to prevent soil splash.

Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Caused by Phytophthora infestans. Spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather (10-24C).
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Greasy water-soaked patches on leaves turning brown-black rapidly. White sporulation on leaf undersides. Fruit shows brown to olive-green firm lesions.
chemical_treatments: URGENT: Spray Metalaxyl-M 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L immediately
Apply Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 3 g/L every 5-7 days
Use Propamocarb 72.2% SL @ 2 ml/L for severe cases
organic_treatments: Bordeaux mixture (1:1:100) spray immediately
Remove and burn all infected plant parts
Improve field drainage
Avoid overhead irrigation
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Use certified transplants. Avoid evening irrigation.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.cause: Caused by Passalora fulva fungus. Thrives in high humidity (85%+) with moderate temperatures.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on upper leaf surface. Olive-green to brown velvety mold on leaf undersides.
chemical_treatments: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L water every 7-10 days
Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L
Use Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5 ml/L for systemic control
organic_treatments: Reduce greenhouse humidity by improving ventilation
Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L spray
Remove infected leaves and dispose properly
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Reduce relative humidity below 85%.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Caused by Septoria lycopersici fungus. Spreads in warm (20-25C) wet conditions via water splash.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Circular spots with dark brown border and light gray center on lower leaves. Small black specks (pycnidia) visible in center of spots.
chemical_treatments: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L water every 7-10 days
Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L as protective spray
Use Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L for systemic control
organic_treatments: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves at first sign
Copper-based fungicide spray (Bordeaux mixture)
Mulch around plants to prevent soil splash
Avoid wetting foliage when irrigating
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Crop rotation 3 years. Certified disease-free seeds. Stake plants for air circulation.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.cause: Infestation by Tetranychus urticae (two-spotted spider mite). Thrives in hot, dry conditions.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Tiny yellow speckles on upper leaf surface. Leaves turn bronze/yellow and drop. Fine webbing on leaf undersides.
chemical_treatments: Spray Abamectin 1.8% EC @ 0.5 ml/L water — highly effective miticide
Apply Bifenazate 24% SC @ 1.5 ml/L for resistant populations
Use Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 0.5 ml/L for all life stages
organic_treatments: Neem oil 10ml/L water spray thoroughly on leaf undersides
Insecticidal soap spray 5ml/L water every 5-7 days
Release predatory mites Phytoseiulus persimilis (biocontrol)
Strong water spray to wash mites off leaves
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Avoid drought stress. Reduce dust on plants. Monitor regularly with hand lens.

Tomato___Target_Spot.cause: Caused by Corynespora cassiicola fungus. Common in tropical and subtropical regions.
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Circular spots with concentric rings (target pattern). Yellow halo around brown lesions. Affects leaves, stems, and fruit.
chemical_treatments: Apply Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L water every 14 days
Spray Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5 ml/L
organic_treatments: Remove and destroy infected plant material
Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L spray
Improve air circulation by pruning and staking
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Crop rotation. Remove crop debris after harvest.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Caused by TYLCV virus, transmitted by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). Incurable once infected.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of leaves. Yellowing of leaf margins. Stunted plant growth. Flowers drop before fruit set.
chemical_treatments: FOCUS ON VECTOR CONTROL: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5 ml/L on whiteflies
Apply Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L for whitefly control
Use yellow sticky traps (45/hectare) to monitor and trap whiteflies
organic_treatments: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately to prevent spread
Neem oil 5ml/L spray to repel whiteflies
Reflective mulches (silver/aluminum) to deter whitefly landing
Release Encarsia formosa (parasitic wasp) for biological control
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Plant resistant TYLCV-tolerant varieties. Use insect-proof nets. Control whiteflies.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Caused by Tomato mosaic virus (ToMV). Spread by contact — contaminated hands, tools, or seeds.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mosaic pattern of light and dark green on leaves. Leaf distortion and curling. Stunted growth. Reduced fruit yield.
chemical_treatments: No chemical cure for viral disease
Remove and destroy infected plants to prevent spread
Disinfect all tools with 10% bleach or 70% alcohol solution
organic_treatments: Wash hands thoroughly before and after handling plants
Remove infected plants immediately and bag for disposal
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use virus-resistant certified seeds. Disinfect tools. Avoid tobacco. Do not transplant suspect seedlings.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with normal green foliage and good fruit development.
chemical_treatments: No treatment needed — plant is healthy!
organic_treatments: Continue regular fertilization with balanced NPK
Proper staking and pruning for air circulation
Monitor weekly for early signs of pests or disease
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Regular monitoring, proper spacing, mulching, and drip irrigation.
